extraction.name: PIQA
extraction.description: PIQA is a benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning. Given a physical goal expressed in natural language, a model must choose the most sensible solution, testing whether language models can link text to an intuitive physics model of the world.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk; Rowan Zellers; Ronan Le Bras; Jianfeng Gao; Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected by prompting human annotators with links to Instructables how-to instructions, asking them to derive or be inspired by an instructable to create a physical goal, a valid solution, and an invalid permutation of that solution.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Crowdsourced how-to instructions from instructables.com, including instruction pages that often contain images or videos for each step and lists of required tools.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were prompted with links to Instructables and asked to create goal-solution pairs: articulate a physical goal, write a valid solution, and provide a subtly invalid permutation ('trick'). Qualification HITs were used before the main task, and separate validation HITs were run afterward; low-agreement examples were removed and low-agreement annotators were de-qualified.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Validation based on annotator agreement; examples with low agreement were removed, and users with low agreement were de-qualified. Qualification required >80% accuracy on identifying well-formed pairs.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper identifies reporting bias in language as a source of bias affecting physical commonsense knowledge, since such facts are rarely explicitly stated in text.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset and task are limited in that some items judged as errors may actually be correct and require external verification, examples were truncated at 150 tokens for 1% of the data, and the authors emphasize that learning physical knowledge from language alone is limiting.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper frames physical commonsense reasoning as important for everyday human problem solving and for progress toward AI systems and robots that can interact with the world and understand language.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: PIQA is introduced as a benchmark dataset for evaluating language representations and pretrained models on physical commonsense reasoning, and as a diagnostic tool to analyze what physical knowledge models can learn from language alone.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Adversarial filtering with AFLite was used to automatically produce the train, development, and test folds; the dataset was also constructed to be adversarial to BERT.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For analysis, strings were tokenized, lowercased, and punctuation was removed before computing edit distance. For modeling, examples were truncated at 150 tokens.
